routes.label: Count contacts and build an example

question: A plastic snap-together cube has a protruding snap on one side and receptacle holes on the other five sides. What is the smallest number of these cubes that can be snapped together so that only receptacle holes are showing?
solution:
Use the standard model of congruent cubes joined face to face without overlap. Each shared pair of faces can hide at most one snap, because a snap must meet a receptacle hole. Thus we need enough face contacts to hide one snap from every cube.

One cube leaves its snap exposed. Two cubes have at most one face contact, so they cannot hide both snaps.

Three cubes have at most two face contacts. To have three contacts, every pair would have to share a face. But consider two cubes touching different faces of a third cube. If those faces are opposite, the two cubes are separated by the third. If the faces are adjacent, the two cubes meet only along an edge. In neither case do they share a face. Therefore three cubes cannot hide all three snaps.

Now place four cubes in a \(2\times2\) square, one cube thick. Going around the square, point each cube's snap into the next cube. Each receiving face has a hole, since that cube's own snap points toward its other neighbor. All four snaps are hidden, and every exposed face has a receptacle hole.

Therefore the smallest number is \(\boxed{4}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
